our_interpretation: Assess capabilities current in the quarter up to the post: July 1 through September 29, 2025. Technical capabilities have no standard reporting period, so this is an explicit evaluator-selected window.

Substantive repository maintenance, debugging, testing, and feature implementation count as engineering tasks. Success on them does not establish the ability to take responsibility for an entire engineering job.
The passage combines a categorical inability claim with narrower concerns about reliability and context handling. These components can receive different evidential assessments.
Learning and adaptation are read operationally as using codebase context and feedback, rather than requiring human-like understanding or automatic changes to model weights.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled evaluations and deployment evidence show the asserted maintenance, adaptation, and context limitations. Supporting the complete causal claim would additionally require showing that those limitations prevent software engineering.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reproducible success on substantive repository engineering tasks contradicts categorical inability. Demonstrated adaptation or controlled absence of the asserted context degradation would contradict the corresponding limitations.

evidence.explanation: Agents successfully resolved a subset of repository-level maintenance and feature tasks under executable tests, contradicting literal inability to perform engineering tasks. The low success rates do not demonstrate reliable whole-job autonomy.

The August survey supports the narrower concern that dependable delegation remained limited and human supervision mattered. It does not support categorical inability, inability to adapt, or an inherent permanent barrier.
